STRIDE, which analyzes each diagram element for six threat types
DREAD, which provides a scoring formula only
PASTA, a seven-stage risk-centric method
questions.explanation: PASTA is risk-centric and attack-simulation based, linking technical threats to business impact through seven stages. STRIDE and DREAD are narrower, and Trike is a risk-based approach that does model threats against assets, so the claim that it excludes attackers is wrong.

questions.question: During threat modeling on a data flow diagram, where should the team concentrate FIRST?
options: On flows that cross trust boundaries, because data changes trust level there
On the user interface colors and layout, because users see them first
On the oldest components, because age alone indicates exposure
On flows entirely inside a single process, because they are the most numerous
questions.explanation: Threats cluster where data passes between zones with different trust or privilege, such as from the internet into the application or from the application into the database. Internal flows, interface appearance and age are less reliable indicators of exposure.

questions.question: A company uses a VPN so that any device on the internal network can reach the HR system without further checks. Which change best aligns with zero trust?
options: Add a second perimeter firewall in front of the existing first one
Authorize every request using identity, device and context
Hide the HR system address from the internal DNS records
Extend the VPN so that contractors and partners can use it as well
questions.explanation: Zero trust removes implicit trust from network location and evaluates every request against identity, device state and policy. Another firewall and a wider VPN keep the perimeter model, and hiding a DNS record is obscurity rather than an access decision.

questions.question: A microservices system authenticates users at the API gateway, and internal services trust any call that reaches them. What is the MOST significant weakness?
options: Anyone inside the network can call any service without being checked
Logs cannot be correlated across the different services at all
Individual services will not be able to scale horizontally under load
The gateway cannot terminate TLS connections coming from external users
questions.explanation: If internal services trust all callers, a single compromised component or network foothold gives access to every service. Design should authenticate service identities (for example with mutual TLS) and authorize in each service. The other issues are unrelated to the trust model.

questions.question: An API endpoint returns an order when called with an order identifier. A tester changes the identifier to another customer order number and receives that order. Which API design flaw is this?
options: Excessive rate limiting, which ended up exposing the order data
Broken object level authorization: ownership is never checked
Broken authentication, since the tester had no account at all
Insufficient logging, which causes the identifiers to be exposed
questions.explanation: The caller is authenticated but the API does not verify the caller is allowed to access that specific object, which is object level authorization. Rate limiting does not expose data, the tester did have valid credentials in this scenario, and logging does not cause the data exposure.

questions.question: A company moves a workload to a platform as a service offering. Which responsibility remains with the customer?
options: Providing physical access control for the provider datacenters
Securing its own code, data, identities and configuration
Patching the underlying hypervisor and the physical hosts
Maintaining redundancy of the provider network backbone
questions.explanation: In the shared responsibility model the provider manages the infrastructure and platform layers, while the customer is always responsible for their data, identities, access configuration and the code they deploy. Hypervisor patching, physical security and the backbone are provider responsibilities.

questions.question: A team builds a container image for a customer-facing service. Which design choice BEST reduces risk?
options: An image with credentials baked in so deployment needs no further configuration
A full operating system image that includes the debugging tools for convenience
An image that runs as root so that file permissions are simpler to manage
A minimal scanned image run as non-root, with secrets injected at runtime
questions.explanation: Smaller images have fewer components to be vulnerable, scanning finds known flaws, non-root limits what a compromise can do, and runtime secrets keep credentials out of the image. Extra tools, root and embedded credentials each enlarge the attack surface or leak secrets.

questions.question: A designer wants single sign-on across several applications and needs a protocol that carries the identity of the authenticated user on top of OAuth 2.0. Which is correct?
options: OpenID Connect
Kerberos with a shared service account
Basic authentication over HTTPS
The OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow alone
questions.explanation: OpenID Connect adds an identity layer, with an ID token about the authenticated user, over OAuth 2.0. OAuth 2.0 alone is for delegated authorization, not authentication, Kerberos with a shared account does not provide federated identity of this kind, and Basic authentication sends credentials with every request.

questions.question: A design review finds that sensitive keys will be stored in the same database as the encrypted data they protect. What is the BEST recommendation?
options: Hold keys in a separate key service or hardware module
Keep the keys where they are but raise the database backup frequency
Rename the key column so the keys are harder for an attacker to find
Encrypt the key using the same key to double the protection it provides
questions.explanation: Separating key management from the data means an attacker who gets the data does not automatically get the means to decrypt it, and key services provide rotation, access control and audit. Renaming is obscurity, self-encryption is circular, and more backups would spread the keys further.

questions.question: A search page builds its database query by concatenating the search text into the SQL statement. Which fix is the MOST effective?
options: Strip single quotes out of the input before it is concatenated
Show a generic message whenever the database query fails
Use parameterized queries so that input is always treated as data
Hide the search page behind a very long and unpredictable URL
questions.explanation: Parameterization separates code and data so the database never interprets input as SQL syntax, which solves the problem at its root. Stripping quotes is a fragile block-list, an obscure URL provides no protection, and hiding errors does not stop injection.

questions.question: A comment field echoes user input inside an HTML page, and a tester inserts script that runs in other users browsers. Which control is the PRIMARY defense?
options: Encrypting the database column that stores the comments
Context-aware output encoding when the data is rendered
Requiring all users to change their passwords more often
Raising the maximum length allowed for the comment field
questions.explanation: Cross-site scripting is prevented chiefly by encoding output for its context so the browser treats it as text, with input validation and a content security policy as additional layers. Encryption at rest, a longer field and password rotation do not stop script execution in the browser.

questions.question: A banking site relies on session cookies. An attacker lures a logged-in user to a page that silently submits a transfer request to the bank. Which defense directly addresses this?
options: Hashing the session identifier in the database
Limiting the number of failed logins
Output encoding of the account number
Anti-forgery tokens plus SameSite cookies
questions.explanation: Cross-site request forgery depends on the browser automatically attaching cookies, so a per-request unpredictable token and SameSite cookies defeat it. Output encoding is for script injection, hashing session identifiers protects them in storage, and login throttling targets guessing attacks.

questions.question: A developer must store user passwords. Which approach is BEST?
options: Hash each password with a unique salt using Argon2id or bcrypt
Store the passwords in plain text inside a well access-controlled database
Encrypt the passwords with AES so that they can be recovered when forgotten
Hash every password with plain SHA-256 and without any salt
questions.explanation: Passwords never need to be recovered, so they should be hashed with a unique salt and a deliberately slow, memory-hard algorithm to make offline guessing expensive. Reversible encryption exposes all passwords if the key is taken, unsalted fast hashes are cracked quickly with tables and GPUs, and plain text is unacceptable.

questions.question: A scan of the repository history shows a cloud access key committed six months ago and removed the next day. What should be done?
options: Add a comment to the code warning developers never to commit any keys
Rewrite the repository history and carry on using the same key
Do nothing, since the key was removed from the current version of the code
Revoke and rotate the key, and adopt a secrets manager with scanning
questions.explanation: Anything committed to version control may have been copied or cached, so the secret must be revoked and replaced regardless of deletion. A secrets manager and automated secret scanning address the root cause. Removing it from the current version or merely rewriting history cannot undo any copies, and a comment is not a control.

questions.question: A C program copies user input into a 64-byte array with an unchecked function. Which long-term action BEST reduces this class of vulnerability?
options: Use bounds checking and move the component to a memory-safe language
Enable verbose error messages so that overflows are easier to diagnose
Rely only on address space layout randomization to stop exploitation
Run the program only during off-peak hours when traffic is low
questions.explanation: Bounds checking removes the bug, and memory-safe languages eliminate whole classes of memory errors. Randomization is a mitigation that raises the difficulty of exploitation without fixing the flaw, verbose errors leak information, and timing has no effect on exploitability.

questions.question: An application checks that a file is writable by the user and then, in a separate step, opens it for writing. An attacker swaps the file for a link to a system file between the two steps. What flaw is this?
options: A cross-site request forgery weakness
An insecure direct object reference in the URL
A buffer over-read in the file system driver
A time-of-check to time-of-use race condition
questions.explanation: The state checked is not the state used because it changed between the check and the use, which is the definition of TOCTOU. Fixing it means performing the check and use atomically on the same handle. The other options describe different weakness categories.

questions.question: A web application shows users a full stack trace and the database query when an error occurs. What is the BEST remediation?
options: Remove logging from the application so that no details exist anywhere
Show the stack trace only to users who have logged in to the application
Encode the stack trace so that it is harder for a casual visitor to read
Show users a generic message and keep the details in protected logs
questions.explanation: Detailed errors reveal internals useful to attackers, while developers still need diagnostics, so keep them in protected logs and give users a generic message. Showing traces to logged-in users still leaks to any account holder, encoding does not help, and removing logs destroys accountability.

questions.question: A reviewer wants to find authorization logic flaws and design mistakes in a new module, not only pattern-based bugs. Which review approach is BEST?
options: A spelling and style check of the comments and identifiers in the source code
A static analysis scan run with the default rule set and no further review
A vulnerability scan of the production network performed by the operations team
Manual secure review by an experienced reviewer, complemented by automated tools
questions.explanation: Business logic and authorization flaws need human understanding of intent, and tools add breadth for known patterns, so a combination is strongest. A default scan misses logic flaws, a network vulnerability scan does not examine code logic, and comments are not security relevant.

questions.question: A team wants to ensure no single compromised developer account can push malicious code to the main branch. Which control is MOST effective?
options: A single shared team account that all of the developers log in with
Branch protection requiring an independent approved review, with signed commits
A weekly email asking developers to confirm that their commits are legitimate
Disabling the audit log in order to save repository storage space
questions.explanation: Requiring independent review enforces separation of duties so one account cannot merge alone, and signed commits tie changes to identities. Shared accounts destroy accountability, an email confirmation is not an enforcement, and removing logs weakens detection.

questions.question: A server component fetches any URL supplied by the user and returns the content. An attacker supplies an internal cloud metadata address and receives credentials. Which weakness is this?
options: Cross-site scripting
SQL injection
Server-side request forgery
Session fixation
questions.explanation: The server is tricked into making a request to a destination chosen by the attacker, reaching internal resources. Defenses include allow-listing destinations and blocking internal ranges. XSS targets browsers, SQL injection targets databases, and session fixation concerns session identifiers.

questions.question: A team has the full source code of a new service and wants to find flaws before it is deployed anywhere. Which testing type is the BEST starting point?
options: Static application security testing
A distributed denial of service simulation
Dynamic application security testing against production
A bug bounty program
questions.explanation: Static analysis examines code without running it, so it can start as soon as code exists and points to the exact location. Dynamic testing needs a running application, a bounty program is run on live systems, and a denial of service simulation tests resilience rather than code flaws.

questions.question: A vendor delivered only a compiled web application running in a staging environment, with no source code. Which technique can find vulnerabilities?
options: A code review of the branching strategy
Dynamic application security testing from the outside
Static analysis of the source code
Software composition analysis of the source repository
questions.explanation: DAST interacts with a running application like an attacker and requires no source, which fits this case. Source-based techniques are not possible without the code or repository.

questions.question: A team wants accurate findings with few false positives by observing code behavior from inside the application while functional tests run. Which technology fits?
options: A network port scanner pointed at the application servers
Interactive testing with an instrumented agent
A web application firewall configured in blocking mode
A source line counter run against the repository on each build
questions.explanation: IAST places sensors in the running application so findings are tied to actual code paths exercised by tests. A port scanner only sees network exposure, a firewall is a protective control rather than a test, and a line counter measures size.

questions.question: A parser for a binary file format has crashed unpredictably in production after receiving unusual files. Which technique is MOST likely to find similar flaws before release?
options: Coverage-guided fuzz testing with malformed inputs
Reviewing the user interface for accessibility problems
Scanning every dependency for outdated version numbers
Checking that the code follows the team naming conventions
questions.explanation: Fuzzing generates large numbers of malformed inputs to provoke crashes and memory errors, and is especially effective on parsers. Dependency scanning, accessibility reviews and naming checks do not exercise the parser with hostile data.

questions.question: A company hires an outside firm to attempt to break into its application. What must be in place BEFORE testing starts?
options: A promise from the testers to fix any vulnerabilities they find
Written authorization and agreed rules of engagement for the work
Disabling all the monitoring so testers can work unobserved
Production database credentials given to the testers in advance
questions.explanation: Written authorization and agreed rules protect both parties and prevent accidental damage or legal exposure by defining what is in scope. Testers do not fix flaws, disabling monitoring defeats part of what is being validated, and unneeded credentials are not a prerequisite.

questions.question: A manager asks why the team runs both vulnerability scans and annual penetration tests. What is the BEST explanation?
options: Scans give frequent breadth over known weaknesses; pen tests show chained exploits
They are the same activity, repeated twice to satisfy the auditors
Scans exploit the weaknesses they find, while penetration tests only list them
Penetration tests replace scans whenever the testing budget is limited
questions.explanation: Automated scans are cheap and repeatable and find known issues, while penetration testing is a skilled attempt to exploit and combine flaws to demonstrate real impact. The roles in the other statements are reversed, identical or incorrectly substituted.

questions.question: A company copies its production customer database into a test environment to make tests more realistic. What is the BEST control?
options: Leave it unchanged, because the test network is internal
Tell the testers not to look at the personal data fields
Encrypt the test database but keep the real values inside it
Use synthetic data, or mask and anonymize the data first
questions.explanation: Test environments typically have weaker controls, so real personal data must not be there unmasked. Synthetic or masked data keeps tests useful and reduces breach and compliance exposure. An internal network, verbal instructions or encryption alone do not remove the exposure.

questions.question: A static scanner reports hundreds of findings, many of which turn out not to be real. What is the BEST response?
options: Fix every finding in order without first checking whether it is real
Disable the tool because false positives make its results worthless
Mark every finding as accepted risk to clear the backlog quickly
Tune the rules and triage by risk instead of ignoring the tool
questions.explanation: False positives are normal and are managed by tuning and triage; ignoring the tool risks false negatives from real flaws that get missed. Blanket acceptance without assessment is not a legitimate risk decision, and fixing all findings blindly wastes effort.

questions.question: A critical vulnerability was fixed last quarter and appears again after a refactor. What practice would MOST directly prevent that?
options: Train developers on the organization password policy
Raise code coverage targets for modules unrelated to the fix
Move the application to a different hosting region
Add an automated regression test for that exact vulnerability
questions.explanation: A regression test that exercises the exact flaw fails the build if it returns. Coverage numbers on unrelated code, password training and moving regions do not guard against reintroducing that defect.

questions.question: Release criteria require no open critical vulnerabilities, but one remains the day before launch and the business wants to proceed. What is the appropriate action?
options: Get documented acceptance from the accountable owner, with mitigations
Remove the vulnerability from the report so that the launch is not delayed
Have the project manager approve the exception quietly and note it in the plan
Reclassify the vulnerability as low severity so the release criteria are met
questions.explanation: Releasing with a known critical flaw is a business risk decision that belongs to the accountable owner, made with full information and recorded with mitigations and a plan. Silent exceptions, reclassification and omission undermine integrity of the process.

questions.question: A team wants to confirm that its new login feature rejects hostile behavior, such as repeated guesses, tampered tokens and skipped steps. Which testing style does this describe?
options: Compatibility testing across browsers
Usability testing of the login page
Load testing to find the throughput limit
Negative testing based on abuse cases
questions.explanation: Negative testing deliberately applies invalid and hostile input and actions to confirm that they are safely refused, often derived from abuse cases. The others test performance, usability and compatibility rather than hostile behavior.

questions.question: A build server produces release packages that are installed by thousands of customers. Which control BEST lets customers verify that a package really came from the vendor and was not altered?
options: Post a checksum on the same download page that serves the package
Digitally sign the artifact and publish the verification certificate
Rename the file with a random version number for each customer
Compress the package with a password that is shared by email
questions.explanation: A digital signature binds the artifact to the publisher and detects tampering, and customers verify it with the published key or certificate. A checksum stored next to the file can be replaced by an attacker, and password compression and renaming do not establish origin or integrity.

questions.question: An organization wants to limit exposure if a new version has a hidden flaw. Which deployment technique is BEST?
options: Skipping the staging environment in order to reduce cost
A canary release to a small share of users first
Disabling monitoring until the release has settled in
Deploying to every user at once so the rollout finishes quickly
questions.explanation: A canary release limits who is affected and provides the chance to detect problems and roll back before wider exposure. Full deployment, skipping staging and disabling monitoring all increase risk.

questions.question: A review of the delivery pipeline finds that all builds use a long-lived administrator credential stored in the pipeline settings. Which change is MOST important?
options: Store the credential in the source repository so it is always available
Rename the credential so that its administrative purpose is not obvious
Share the credential with the operations team to provide some redundancy
Use short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials issued per build
questions.explanation: The pipeline is a high-value target, so credentials should be minimal, temporary and protected, limiting damage if a build is compromised. Renaming gives no protection, sharing widens exposure and storing it in the repository leaks it.

questions.question: Three vulnerabilities are open: a CVSS 9.8 flaw in an internal tool with no network exposure, a CVSS 7.5 flaw in an internet-facing service listed in the known exploited vulnerabilities catalog, and a CVSS 5.0 flaw in a test server. Which should be addressed FIRST?
options: The 9.8 flaw in the internal tool, because its base score is the highest
The 7.5 flaw in the internet-facing service being exploited in the wild
The 5.0 flaw in the test server, because it will be the quickest to fix
All three at the same time, in whatever order the team happens to choose
questions.explanation: Prioritization should combine severity with exposure and exploitation evidence, and active exploitation of an internet-facing system makes the risk immediate. Base score alone ignores context, ease of fixing is not a risk criterion, and refusing to prioritize wastes scarce effort.

questions.question: A vendor receives a report of a serious flaw from an outside researcher. What is the BEST first step?
options: Require the researcher to sign an agreement that bans any future disclosure
Ignore the report until a customer complains about the same behavior
Acknowledge and validate the report, then coordinate the fix with the reporter
Publish the technical details at once so that customers can protect themselves
questions.explanation: A coordinated disclosure process acknowledges, validates and fixes the issue while agreeing a timeline with the reporter. Ignoring invites public disclosure, permanent gag demands damage trust, and publishing details before a fix exposes customers.

questions.question: A critical patch cannot be applied for two weeks because it requires a long testing cycle on a legacy system. What is the BEST interim step?
options: Apply the patch to production without any testing in order to close it
Turn off the logging that reports the vulnerability on the system
Apply compensating controls such as virtual patching
Ignore the vulnerability and take no action until the patch is ready
questions.explanation: Compensating controls reduce exposure while the patch is validated, and a documented exception keeps accountability. Ignoring it leaves the risk open, untested patches can break production, and disabling logging hides evidence.

questions.question: A software product reaches its end-of-life date, and the vendor will stop issuing patches. Which action is MOST appropriate for a customer who depends on it?
options: Remove its logging in order to improve the performance of the system
Continue using it indefinitely on the grounds that it still works correctly
Plan migration to a supported product and add compensating controls meanwhile
Wait until a breach occurs before beginning any planning for the change
questions.explanation: Unsupported software accumulates unfixable vulnerabilities, so the right response is to plan retirement or replacement and isolate or protect the system meanwhile. Using it indefinitely, reducing logging and waiting for a breach all raise risk.

questions.question: Retired application servers are being returned to a leasing company. They held confidential records. Which action is MOST appropriate?
options: Format the disks with a quick format and reinstall a clean operating system
Delete the files and empty the recycle bin on each server before return
Remove the asset labels from the servers so they are not identifiable
Sanitize the media with a method suited to its sensitivity, and keep a record
questions.explanation: Sanitization must make data unrecoverable in line with NIST SP 800-88, and records show it was done. Deleting files or quick formatting leaves recoverable data, and removing labels has no effect on data.

questions.question: A new vulnerability is announced in a widely used logging library. What is the BEST way to find out quickly which products are affected?
options: Wait until customers start to report problems with the products they use
Run a performance test on every product in the portfolio
Review the marketing material for each of the company products
Query the software bill of materials inventory for the library and version
questions.explanation: An SBOM is exactly the inventory that lets an organization find where a component is used and act fast. Waiting for customers, reading marketing material and running performance tests do not reveal what is inside the software.

questions.question: An SBOM shows a component with a critical vulnerability, but the supplier states that the vulnerable function is never reachable in the product. Which artifact communicates this?
options: A Common Criteria Protection Profile
A software escrow agreement
A penetration test report summary
A VEX statement
questions.explanation: A VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) document tells consumers whether a known vulnerability actually affects a product, reducing false alarms from SBOM matching. The others are about continuity, evaluation baselines and test results, not exploitability of a specific component vulnerability.

questions.question: A company builds software from internal packages named in a private registry. An attacker publishes a public package with the same name and a higher version number, and the build starts using it. What is this attack?
options: Cross-site scripting
A man-in-the-middle attack on the build network
Typosquatting
Dependency confusion
questions.explanation: Dependency confusion exploits package managers that prefer the highest version across registries, so a public package shadows the internal one. Typosquatting relies on misspelled names, which is not happening here, and the others are unrelated attack classes.

questions.question: A team wants to detect newly disclosed vulnerabilities and license problems in the open-source libraries its application uses. Which tool category fits?
options: Software composition analysis
Fuzz testing of the application input handlers
Network intrusion detection on the production segment
Static application security testing of the code the team wrote
questions.explanation: SCA identifies third-party and open-source components, their versions, known vulnerabilities and licenses. SAST analyzes the code the team wrote, fuzzing sends malformed input to your code, and intrusion detection monitors network traffic.

questions.question: A proprietary product plans to include a library under a copyleft license that requires derived works to be released under the same license. Which risk should be assessed FIRST?
options: Usability risk arising from the quality of the library documentation
Performance risk from the additional size of the library at runtime
Licensing risk of having to release under copyleft terms
Availability risk arising from the update schedule of the library
questions.explanation: Copyleft terms can oblige distributors to share source code of derivative works, which could conflict with a proprietary model, so license review comes before adoption. The other risks are real but are not the defining concern for this license type.

questions.question: A company must buy a critical component from a new supplier. Which action provides the MOST enforceable assurance of the supplier security practices?
options: Choose whichever supplier offers the component at the lowest price
Put security, breach notification and audit terms in the contract
Ask the supplier to complete a short informal questionnaire by telephone
Rely on the security statements published on the supplier marketing page
questions.explanation: Contract terms are enforceable and give the buyer recourse, and a right to audit lets them verify claims. Marketing, verbal assurances and price offer no enforceable security commitment.

questions.question: A customer needs assurance that it can keep maintaining a mission-critical custom application if the vendor goes out of business. Which arrangement addresses this?
options: A non-disclosure agreement signed by the key vendor staff members
A longer warranty on the hardware that the application runs on
An additional penetration test carried out each year by an outside firm
Software escrow, with the deposit verified to build correctly
questions.explanation: Escrow releases source code and build materials to the customer upon defined events such as insolvency, and verification confirms the deposit is usable. Hardware warranties, NDAs and penetration tests do not preserve the ability to maintain the software.

questions.question: A buyer is comparing two products evaluated under Common Criteria, one at EAL2 and one at EAL4. What does the higher level indicate?
options: A guarantee that the product contains no remaining vulnerabilities
Certification of the vendor to handle all classified information
More rigorous evaluation of design, testing and development processes
A larger number of security features is built into the product
questions.explanation: An evaluation assurance level measures the depth and rigor of evaluation against the Security Target, not how many features the product has. No level guarantees absence of vulnerabilities, and the level is unrelated to handling classified information.

questions.question: Which TWO principles are both violated when a web service runs as an administrator and also skips authorization checks on internal calls because the caller is on the internal network? (Choose two.)
options: Economy of mechanism
Least privilege
Complete mediation
Open design
Psychological acceptability
questions.explanation: Running with administrator rights gives the service more access than it needs, which violates least privilege, and trusting internal callers without checking each access violates complete mediation. Psychological acceptability concerns usability, open design concerns secrecy of the design, and economy of mechanism concerns simplicity, none of which are described.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about risk treatment are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Accepting a risk should be a documented decision by an accountable owner who understands the exposure
Mitigating a risk eliminates the threat completely
Avoiding a risk means installing a control that reduces its likelihood
Accepting a risk is the default outcome when no one responds to a finding
Transferring risk, such as through insurance or a contract, shifts financial impact but not the accountability for the decision
questions.explanation: Transfer moves some financial consequence to another party while the organization remains accountable, and acceptance is only valid when an informed owner decides and records it. Avoidance means stopping the risky activity rather than adding a control, mitigation reduces but does not eliminate risk, and inaction is not an informed acceptance.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following are prescriptive frameworks that tell an organization what secure development activities to adopt? (Choose two.)
options: CVSS
BSIMM
NIST SSDF
OWASP SAMM
SPDX
questions.explanation: SAMM and the SSDF prescribe practices and, in SAMM, maturity levels to aim for. BSIMM is descriptive and reports what other organizations do, CVSS scores vulnerability severity, and SPDX is a format for software inventories.

questions.question: Which TWO actions BEST adapt a secure SDLC to a fast agile and DevOps delivery model? (Choose two.)
options: Move security requirements into a document that is not updated
Require a signed paper approval from the board before every sprint
Add security acceptance criteria to the definition of done for each story
Embed automated static analysis and dependency scanning in the pipeline
Perform one manual penetration test at the end of the project
questions.explanation: Automated checks and testable acceptance criteria scale with fast iteration and provide continuous feedback. A single end-of-project test, per-sprint board approval and a static requirements document either arrive too late or are impractical at that speed.

questions.question: Which TWO factors should drive the security requirements for an application that stores health records of patients in several countries? (Choose two.)
options: The data classification and sensitivity of the records
The color scheme of the user interface
The privacy and health laws that apply to those patients
The vendor of the monitors in the office
The preferred programming language of the team
questions.explanation: Requirements come from what the data is and what laws and contracts govern it. Language preference, interface design and office equipment can influence implementation but do not set the required security and privacy controls.

questions.question: Which THREE items would normally be captured in logging requirements for an application? (Choose three.)
options: Which security events must be recorded, such as login failures and privilege changes
That every user keystroke must be recorded in plain text
That logs may be edited by developers to remove embarrassing entries
That passwords and full payment card numbers must never be written to logs
How long logs must be retained and how they are protected from tampering
questions.explanation: Good logging requirements say what to log, how long to keep it and how to protect it, and exclude sensitive data. Recording all keystrokes creates a privacy and security hazard and editable logs defeat accountability.

questions.question: Which TWO are valid sources of abuse and misuse cases? (Choose two.)
options: Outputs of threat modeling for the same feature
The firmware version of the build server
The monthly cloud billing report
Brainstorming with stakeholders about how an attacker would subvert a feature
questions.explanation: Abuse cases come from adversarial thinking and structured threat analysis of the feature. Billing reports and build server firmware have no direct connection to how a feature could be abused.

questions.question: Which TWO are benefits of attack surface reduction? (Choose two.)
options: Removal of the need for authentication on remaining features
A guarantee that no vulnerabilities remain
Fewer entry points that an attacker can probe
Automatic compliance with every regulation
Less code and configuration to maintain and defend
questions.explanation: Removing unneeded features, ports and accounts shrinks what must be tested and defended. It does not guarantee a vulnerability-free product, it does not remove the need to authenticate the remaining functions, and compliance requires more than a smaller surface.

questions.question: Which TWO design measures address threats of spoofing and elevation of privilege respectively? (Choose two.)
options: Strong authentication, such as multi-factor authentication
Encrypting data at rest
Authorization checks that enforce least privilege on every request
Rate limiting on public endpoints
Digital signatures on log files
questions.explanation: Spoofing is answered by authentication, and elevation of privilege by authorization with least privilege. Signing logs addresses tampering and repudiation, rate limiting addresses denial of service, and encryption at rest addresses information disclosure.

questions.question: Which TWO are appropriate controls when designing a serverless function that processes events from a public queue? (Choose two.)
options: Validate every event as untrusted input
Share one broad administrator role among all the functions
Give each function its own narrowly scoped identity
Embed secrets in the function source for speed
questions.explanation: Event sources are inputs that attackers can influence and per-function identities with minimal permissions limit damage. A shared broad role and embedded secrets both violate least privilege and secrets handling.

questions.question: Which TWO measures together best prevent SQL injection and cross-site scripting in a web application? (Choose two.)
options: Longer session timeouts
Context-aware output encoding when displaying data
Parameterized queries for database access
Hiding the server version banner
Disabling the audit log
questions.explanation: Parameterization prevents data being interpreted as SQL and output encoding prevents data being interpreted as script. Session timeouts, disabled logging and banner hiding do not address either attack at its root.

questions.question: Which TWO are correct practices for secrets management? (Choose two.)
options: Keep secrets in environment-specific configuration files in the repository
Store secrets in a dedicated manager with access control, rotation and auditing
Share one service account password among all developers
Rotate any secret that has ever been committed to a repository
questions.explanation: A secrets manager centralizes control and a leaked secret must be considered compromised. Committing configuration with secrets and sharing one password both create exposure and remove accountability.

questions.question: Which TWO statements correctly contrast static and dynamic application security testing? (Choose two.)
options: Static testing examines code without running it and can identify the line with the flaw
Dynamic testing probes a running application and can reveal runtime and configuration issues
Dynamic testing identifies the exact source file and line for each finding
Static testing requires a deployed environment with user traffic
questions.explanation: Static testing works on code and gives locations, while dynamic testing works on the running system and finds issues visible only at runtime. The reversed statements are common mistakes.

questions.question: Which THREE are characteristics of an effective penetration test engagement? (Choose three.)
options: A report with findings, evidence and remediation advice
Testers who actively attempt to exploit weaknesses to show impact
Immediate public release of findings
A written scope and authorization before testing begins
Testing of any system the testers find, regardless of the scope
questions.explanation: A penetration test is authorized, scoped, exploitation-oriented and ends in actionable reporting. Testing outside the agreed scope can be illegal, and findings are confidential until fixed.

questions.question: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of using test environments? (Choose two.)
options: Use synthetic or masked data in place of production records
Give all employees access for convenience
Keep the test systems unpatched since they are not production
Apply access control and monitoring to test systems
questions.explanation: Test systems often hold copies of real data and are weakly protected, so masking data and applying access control close the gap. Open access and no patching enlarge the exposure.

questions.question: Which TWO are elements of a secure CI/CD pipeline? (Choose two.)
options: Disabling build logging to save storage
A single shared administrator account for every pipeline job
Isolated, ephemeral build runners with short-lived credentials
Signed build artifacts with access-controlled and logged pipeline changes
questions.explanation: Isolation and short-lived credentials limit what a compromised job can do, and signing with controlled changes protects integrity. A shared administrator account and no logs both make compromise easier and harder to detect.

questions.question: Which TWO should be considered when prioritizing which vulnerabilities to fix first? (Choose two.)
options: The exposure and business criticality of the affected system
Which vulnerability was found by the most senior tester
The order in which the findings appear in the report
Evidence that the vulnerability is being actively exploited
questions.explanation: Risk-based prioritization uses exploitation evidence, exposure and criticality in addition to base severity. Who found a flaw and report order say nothing about risk.

questions.question: Which TWO are effective defenses against dependency confusion attacks? (Choose two.)
options: Pin dependency versions with lock files and verify package hashes
Allow builds to pull from any public registry in any order
Reserve or scope internal package names and configure the build to resolve them only from the private registry
Always install the latest version of every package automatically
questions.explanation: Controlling where internal names resolve and pinning with hashes stops substitution by a malicious higher-version package. Taking the latest version automatically and unrestricted resolution are the conditions the attack exploits.

questions.question: An application that has successfully authenticated a user has therefore authorized that user to perform any action the application offers.
questions.explanation: Authentication establishes identity only; authorization is a separate decision about what that identity may do, and it must be checked for each request according to the user permissions.

questions.question: Defense in depth means layering independent controls so that the failure of one control does not by itself expose the asset.
questions.explanation: Independent layers, such as input validation, authorization, encryption and monitoring, mean one failure is not enough for compromise. The layers must not share the same weakness or they add little.

questions.question: Encrypting a message with a symmetric key that two parties share provides non-repudiation of who sent it.
questions.explanation: Either holder of the shared key could have produced the message, so neither can be proven to have sent it. Non-repudiation requires something unique to one party, such as an asymmetric digital signature, plus trustworthy logging.

questions.question: Under the open design principle, a well-designed security mechanism should stay secure even if everything about it except the keys is public knowledge.
questions.explanation: Security should rest on protecting keys and other secrets, not on secrecy of the design. Obscurity can be a minor extra layer but fails once the design leaks or is reverse engineered.

questions.question: BSIMM tells an organization which security activities it must perform in order to be compliant.
questions.explanation: BSIMM is descriptive: it reports what participating organizations observably do so a firm can compare itself. Prescriptive models such as SAMM and the SSDF tell organizations what to adopt.

questions.question: Finding and fixing a security defect during requirements or design is generally far cheaper than fixing it after release.
questions.explanation: The cost to correct a defect grows as it moves through the lifecycle, because more work depends on it and deployed fixes require patching and customer disruption. This is the rationale for shifting security left.

questions.question: A security gate that any project manager can routinely waive without recorded justification still provides strong assurance.
questions.explanation: A gate only has value when it has clear criteria and a controlled exception process. Routine, unrecorded waivers mean nobody is actually accountable for the residual risk.

questions.question: Emergency changes may skip change management entirely, since speed is more important than documentation.
questions.explanation: Emergency changes follow an expedited process with delegated approval and are documented and reviewed afterward. Skipping the process removes accountability and the ability to learn from the change.

questions.question: Security requirements are best identified early in the lifecycle, because requirements that are never stated are rarely designed, built or tested.
questions.explanation: Requirements drive design and testing. A control that is not specified is easily missed and expensive to add later.

questions.question: Pseudonymized personal data can usually be re-identified with additional information, so it is generally still treated as personal data under privacy regulations.
questions.explanation: Under regimes such as GDPR pseudonymized data remains personal data because the link to the individual can be restored. Only data that cannot reasonably be re-identified is anonymous.

questions.question: Under FIPS 199, the overall impact category of a system is the highest impact level among confidentiality, integrity and availability.
questions.explanation: The high-water mark rule means a single high impact rating on any of the three properties makes the overall category high, which in turn selects a stronger control baseline.

questions.question: An RTO states how much data loss is tolerable, while an RPO states how long a restoration may take.
questions.explanation: The definitions are reversed. RTO is the maximum acceptable time to restore service and RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as a period of time.

questions.question: STRIDE is used to classify threats into categories, while DREAD is used to rate them so they can be prioritized.
questions.explanation: STRIDE names the categories (spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege) and DREAD scores damage, reproducibility, exploitability, affected users and discoverability. Candidates often swap the two roles.

questions.question: In a zero trust architecture, a request from a device inside the corporate network is trusted by default.
questions.explanation: Zero trust removes implicit trust based on network location. Each request is authenticated, authorized and evaluated using identity, device state and context.

questions.question: OAuth 2.0 on its own is an authorization framework and not an authentication protocol.
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 grants delegated access to resources through tokens. Authentication of the user is provided by a layer above it such as OpenID Connect.

questions.question: Because containers share the host kernel, they generally provide weaker isolation between workloads than separate virtual machines.
questions.explanation: A flaw in the shared kernel can affect every container on the host, so extra measures such as non-root users, restricted capabilities and network policies matter.

questions.question: In a shared responsibility model for cloud, the customer is no longer responsible for its data once it is stored in the provider platform.
questions.explanation: The provider secures the infrastructure and, depending on the service model, parts of the platform, but customers remain responsible for their data, identities, access configuration and the security of their own code.

questions.question: Client-side input validation is sufficient to protect an application from malicious input, because the user interface will reject bad data.
questions.explanation: Attackers can bypass the client entirely and send requests directly, so validation must be enforced on the server. Client-side checks are a usability aid only.

questions.question: Address space layout randomization removes buffer overflow vulnerabilities from a program.
questions.explanation: ASLR makes exploitation harder by randomizing memory layout, but the overflow remains. The fix is bounds checking or using a memory-safe language.

questions.question: Passwords should be stored using a reversible encryption scheme so that support staff can recover them for users who forget them.
questions.explanation: Passwords should be hashed with a unique salt using a slow algorithm. They should never need to be recovered, and reversible storage exposes every password if the key is taken.

questions.question: An access key that was committed to a repository and quickly deleted can safely be considered secret again.
questions.explanation: Clones, caches and history can all retain the value, so the key must be treated as compromised, revoked and rotated.

questions.question: Hiding a link from the user interface is an adequate access control for an administrative function.
questions.explanation: Access control must be enforced on the server for each request. A hidden link can be found or guessed, and an unprotected endpoint can be called directly.

questions.question: Dynamic application security testing can be performed against a running application even when no source code is available.
questions.explanation: DAST works from outside on a running application, like an attacker, and needs no source code. It is static analysis that examines source, and it can point to the line of code.

questions.question: Fuzz testing is particularly effective at finding input handling and memory safety flaws in parsers.
questions.explanation: Fuzzers produce large volumes of malformed input and watch for crashes and hangs, which often indicate memory corruption or unhandled cases.

questions.question: A high code coverage percentage proves that the tests check security behavior correctly.
questions.explanation: Coverage shows which code ran during tests, not whether the tests make meaningful checks. Security test cases must also address abuse cases and error paths.

questions.question: A penetration test may be started on a production system once the testers verbally agree on what to test.
questions.explanation: Testing needs written authorization from the owner and agreed rules of engagement defining scope and limits, to protect both parties and avoid unintended damage.

questions.question: Real production customer data may be loaded into a less protected test environment as long as the test network is internal.
questions.explanation: Test systems typically have weaker controls, so production personal data must be replaced with synthetic or masked data regardless of the network.

questions.question: A digital signature on a software release shows who published it and that it was not altered after signing, but not that it is free of vulnerabilities.
questions.explanation: A signature proves the publisher and integrity since signing. A signed artifact can still contain flaws, or malicious code if the signing process itself was compromised.

questions.question: The CVSS base score alone is a reliable measure of the risk a vulnerability poses to a specific organization.
questions.explanation: CVSS measures intrinsic severity. Risk also depends on exposure, exploitation activity, compensating controls and the criticality of the affected asset.

questions.question: Deleting files or performing a quick format is an acceptable way to sanitize storage that held confidential data before it leaves the organization.
questions.explanation: These actions normally leave recoverable data. Sanitization should follow a method such as NIST SP 800-88 clear, purge or destroy, chosen by data sensitivity and media type.

questions.question: Software that has reached end of life may contain known vulnerabilities that the vendor will no longer fix.
questions.explanation: After end of life the vendor stops providing patches, so newly discovered flaws remain open. Customers must migrate or isolate the software and add compensating controls.

questions.question: An SBOM alone tells an organization whether each listed component is exploitable in the product.
questions.explanation: An SBOM is an inventory of components and versions. Determining exploitability requires vulnerability data and, for example, a VEX statement from the supplier.

questions.question: Dependency pinning and verifying hashes help defend against malicious package substitution.
questions.explanation: Pinned versions with recorded hashes mean the build only accepts the exact artifact that was reviewed, blocking a newly published malicious look-alike or higher version.

questions.question: A higher Common Criteria evaluation assurance level means the product has more security features than a lower-level product.
questions.explanation: The level reflects the rigor and depth of the evaluation, giving more confidence that the stated security functions work, not how many functions exist.

questions.question: A company root signing key can only be activated when any two of five custodians each enter a share of the secret. Which security concepts does this arrangement combine?
options: Defense in depth, achieved by using different vendors for each custodian share
Least privilege, achieved by reducing the run-time privileges of the signing service
Separation of duties, enforced through multi-party control with secret sharing
Complete mediation, achieved by re-checking the key on every signing request
questions.explanation: Requiring several people to act together, with the secret split so that no one holds it all, is multi-party control and secret sharing, a technical form of separation of duties. Diverse vendors would be technical diversity, reducing run-time privileges is least privilege, and rechecking authority on each request is complete mediation, none of which describes the custodian arrangement.

questions.question: A database is replicated to a second site in near real time. A faulty release corrupts many rows and the corruption reaches the replica within seconds. What does this show about replication?
options: It protects integrity because the replica compares itself with the primary and rolls the change back
It protects availability but copies integrity damage, so point-in-time backups are still needed
It makes backups unnecessary because two live copies already exist at independent sites
It works only when clustering is also used to vote on which copy holds the correct values
questions.explanation: Replication keeps copies in step, which helps when a node or site fails, but it faithfully copies bad writes and deletions as well. Recovering from corruption needs backups or versioned storage. Replicas do not automatically roll back changes, two live copies are not a substitute for backups, and clustering is not required to make replication copy changes.

questions.question: An application advertises multi-factor authentication, but it asks for a password and then a security question answer. What is the best assessment?
options: It is true multi-factor authentication because two separate prompts are shown
It is biometric authentication because the answer is personal to the user
It is two-factor authentication as long as the answer is stored as a salted hash
It is single-factor authentication used twice, because both are something the user knows
questions.explanation: Multi-factor authentication needs factors from different categories, such as knowledge, possession and inherence. A password and a security question are both knowledge factors, so they add little. The number of prompts does not matter, a personal answer is not a biometric measurement, and how the answer is stored does not change its factor type.

questions.question: A purchasing system must let auditors show that a named manager approved each large order and cannot later deny it. Which design is the most appropriate?
options: Each approver signs the approval with a private key, and entries go into a tamper-evident log
Each approval is protected with a shared HMAC key that all managers use
Approval records are encrypted in the database with a strong symmetric algorithm
Approvers sign in with a password, and session logs stay editable by database staff
questions.explanation: Non-repudiation needs something unique to the individual, such as an asymmetric digital signature, plus a log that cannot be quietly altered. A shared key means any holder could have produced the approval, encryption provides confidentiality rather than attribution, and logs that administrators can edit cannot be trusted as proof.

questions.question: A product passed its annual compliance audit, yet a penetration test then finds exploitable flaws. Which statement best explains the difference?
options: The penetration test must be wrong because passing the audit proves the software is secure
Compliance frameworks only cover availability, so security flaws are outside their scope
Penetration tests report only theoretical issues, so the findings can be set aside
The audit shows controls existed at a point in time, not current resilience
questions.explanation: Governance, risk and compliance work shows that obligations are met, but compliance is a baseline measured at a point in time and does not guarantee the software withstands today attacks. Audits do not prove security, frameworks are not limited to availability, and exploitable findings are not theoretical.

questions.question: A payment service depends on a single authentication server, and every login fails when it goes down. Which change best applies the resiliency principle without weakening security?
options: Add redundant authentication nodes with failover that still denies on failure
Let users continue with their last session while the server is unavailable
Raise the authentication server timeout so that it can wait longer for a response
Cache successful passwords in each client so logins can be verified locally
questions.explanation: Resiliency removes the single point of failure with redundancy and failover, while the fail-secure default means a failure never grants access. Allowing unauthenticated continuation, caching passwords on clients or merely waiting longer either weaken authentication or leave the single point of failure in place.

questions.question: Which TWO measures make defense-in-depth layers more independent of one another? (Choose two.)
options: Spread critical services across geographically separate sites
Use different technologies or vendors for different protective layers
Host all layers on the same virtualization host to ease monitoring
Run every layer under one shared service account for simpler administration
Standardize on a single product for every layer to cut licensing costs
questions.explanation: Technical diversity means one flaw in one product cannot defeat every layer, and geographic diversity means one site disaster does not take everything. Sharing an account, a host or a product creates a common point of failure that defeats independence even though it is simpler to run.

questions.question: Split knowledge means that two people must act together to complete an operation, which is the same as dual control.
questions.explanation: Split knowledge means no single person knows the whole secret, for example each custodian knows half of a key. Dual control means two people must act together to perform an operation. They are related ways of enforcing separation of duties, but they are not the same, and answer choices often swap them.

questions.question: A biometric template that has leaked can simply be reset, in the same way as a password.
questions.explanation: Biometric characteristics such as fingerprints cannot be changed, so a leaked template cannot be reissued, and matching is probabilistic with false accept and false reject rates. This is why biometrics are usually combined with another factor and the templates are protected carefully.

questions.question: Meeting every regulatory requirement is sufficient evidence that a software product is secure.
questions.explanation: Compliance shows that required controls and processes exist, usually at a point in time. Threats change faster than regulations, so compliance is a baseline rather than proof of security.

questions.question: A pipeline fails builds that contain critical static analysis findings, but a release manager keeps lowering the threshold whenever a deadline approaches. What is the right approach?
options: Remove the build gate and rely on a final manual review of the release
Let the release manager adjust the threshold since the manager owns the schedule
Raise the threshold permanently so the build never fails near a deadline
Set break/build criteria in advance; exceptions go to a named risk owner
questions.explanation: A gate has value only when criteria are set beforehand and exceptions are controlled and recorded by the accountable risk owner. Removing it loses the control, giving the schedule owner the power to move the threshold defeats it, and a permanently raised threshold is simply a weaker control.

questions.question: Which statement is the best example of an objective and key result (OKR) for a software security program?
options: All third-party components must be approved by the architecture board
Lower dependency risk: fix 95 percent of critical flaws in 14 days
A weekly report listing every open vulnerability by application name
A scanner configured to run on every merge request in the repository
questions.explanation: An OKR pairs a goal with measurable results for a period, here fewer exposed dependency flaws and a target fix rate. A mandatory approval rule is a policy, a weekly listing is a report and a scanner schedule is a tool setting, none of which states a measurable outcome.

questions.question: A legacy portal is being retired. Which approach to data disposition is the most appropriate?
options: Destroy all data immediately to remove risk, then ask legal what had to be kept
Archive every record indefinitely in case it proves useful to the business later
Check retention duties, archive what is needed, then destroy and record
Leave the data in place and simply cancel the licenses for the retired portal
questions.explanation: Disposition follows retention rules: confirm what must be kept, archive it, securely destroy the remainder and document the destruction. Destroying first can break legal obligations, keeping everything forever increases breach exposure and violates privacy limits, and leaving data on a retired system leaves unmanaged risk.

questions.question: A company learns on Monday that personal data of EU residents was exposed. By when must the supervisory authority be told under GDPR, where feasible?
options: Within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach
Within 30 days after the forensic investigation is completed
Within 60 calendar days of the discovery date
At the next scheduled annual compliance audit
questions.explanation: GDPR requires notification to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware. The 60-day figure belongs to the US HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, and waiting for a completed investigation or an annual audit would miss the deadline.

questions.question: After the control assessment of a high-impact system, who should grant the authorization to operate?
options: The senior official accountable for business risk
The lead developer, who knows the system better than anyone
The independent assessor who tested the controls
The security champion embedded in the development team
questions.explanation: Authorization is a risk-acceptance decision made on the assessment evidence by someone with authority over the business or mission risk. Developers and security champions are not independent and lack that authority, and the assessor provides the evidence but does not accept the risk.

questions.question: A team confirmed through reviews and traceability that the software matches its signed specification, yet users say it does not solve their real problem. Which activity would have exposed this?
options: Additional static analysis of the source code
A larger penetration test of the deployed system
Validation with representative users
Raising the code coverage target for unit tests
questions.explanation: Verification checks that the product was built right against its specification, and validation checks that the right product was built for real needs. Static analysis, penetration tests and coverage all assess correctness or security against the existing specification and cannot show that the specification itself was wrong.

questions.question: A scanner reports a critical SQL injection in an isolated internal tool used by three staff with no sensitive data, and a medium flaw in the checkout flow. Management asks what to fix first. What is the best approach?
options: Always fix the highest technical severity first, whatever it protects
Fix the checkout issue only, since internal tools never matter to the business
Translate each finding into business risk and let the owner decide
Defer both until the next annual penetration test confirms them
questions.explanation: Technical risk describes the flaw, business risk describes what it means to the organization, and priorities and acceptance belong to those accountable for the business risk. Sorting only by technical score ignores context, declaring internal tools unimportant is an unjustified assumption, and waiting for an annual test leaves known issues untreated.

questions.question: Which TWO are sources of secure development guidance referenced when adopting standards and frameworks? (Choose two.)
options: The CVSS specification
SAFECode fundamental practices for secure software development
ISO/IEC 27034 application security guidance
The CAPTCHA specification
The SPDX specification
questions.explanation: SAFECode publishes practical secure development guidance and ISO/IEC 27034 covers application security processes. CVSS scores vulnerability severity, SPDX describes software bill of materials data and CAPTCHA is a human-versus-bot challenge, so none of those is development guidance.

questions.question: A single annual awareness video satisfies the need for role-based security training for developers, architects and operators.
questions.explanation: Different roles need different skills, such as secure coding for developers, threat modeling for architects and hardening for operators. Awareness raises general behavior, whereas role-based training builds specific skills and must be refreshed.

questions.question: Under the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, affected individuals must be notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery of the breach.
questions.explanation: That is the outer limit in the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule, with discovery starting the clock. GDPR is stricter for the regulator notification at 72 hours, and US state laws can add their own deadlines.

questions.question: Verification confirms that the software meets the real needs of its users, while validation confirms that it matches its written specification.
questions.explanation: The definitions are reversed. Verification asks whether the product was built right against its specification and requirements, and validation asks whether the right product was built for real user needs.

questions.question: A developer asks who decides how customer billing data should be classified. Who is correct?
options: The database administrator who stores and backs up the data
The developer who implements the features that use the data
The cloud provider that hosts the database service
The business data owner who is accountable for the data
questions.explanation: The data owner is the accountable business role that classifies data and approves access. Administrators and developers act as custodians who apply the owner decisions, and a hosting provider does not decide how a customer classifies its own data.

questions.question: Sensitive customer details have spread into spreadsheets, emails and shared folders. What should be done first to define handling requirements?
options: Encrypt the main customer database column by column
Block email attachments across the whole organization
Move all shared folders to a lower-cost storage tier
Discover and classify the unstructured data first
questions.explanation: Unstructured data has no schema, so it must be found and classified before rules can be applied. Encrypting the database does not touch the copies, blocking attachments is a blunt control with no classification basis, and moving storage tiers does not address handling requirements.

questions.question: A team replaces customer names with random identifiers but keeps a mapping table so support staff can look people up. How is the resulting data treated under GDPR?
options: It is pseudonymized and still personal data
It is anonymized and falls outside the regulation
It is aggregated data, which is exempt from the regulation
It is public data, because the names are no longer displayed
questions.explanation: Because the mapping table can restore the link to the individual, the data is only pseudonymized and remains personal data with its protections. Anonymization requires that people cannot reasonably be re-identified. Replacing a name with an identifier does not make data aggregated or public.

questions.question: A privacy requirement states that users can ask for their personal data to be deleted. Which design requirement best makes this achievable?
options: Delete the person data in every store, log and processor
Display a notice that deletion requests can be sent to the support mailbox
Mark the account as inactive and hide it from all screens
Encrypt the data and discard the user password hash
questions.explanation: Erasure works only if the system can find and remove a single person data everywhere it lives, including copies and processors, while recording lawful reasons to keep some of it. A notice, hiding the account or discarding a hash leaves the personal data in place.

questions.question: A software-as-a-service product serves EU and US customers, and EU customers require that their data stays in the EU. Which requirement best expresses this?
options: All traffic uses TLS and the data may be stored in any region
EU tenant data, keys, backups and support access are pinned to EU regions
The terms of service say that data may be moved to any region
Every tenant is replicated to all regions to maximize availability
questions.explanation: Data residency is an architecture requirement that must cover storage, keys, backups and even administrative access. Encrypting traffic does not control location, terms of service cannot override the customer requirement and replicating everywhere breaks it.

questions.question: An audit finds service accounts from a finished project that still have database access. Which missing requirement is the root cause?
options: Longer and more complex passwords for all service accounts
Multi-factor authentication for batch jobs run by service accounts
Named owners and periodic reapproval with removal at project end
A shared service account for all batch jobs in the company
questions.explanation: Access that nobody reapproves only accumulates, so provisioning requirements need ownership, scope, periodic recertification and deprovisioning at the end. Stronger passwords or MFA do not remove access that should not exist, and a shared account would worsen accountability.

questions.question: The architecture board mandates that all new services use one approved cryptographic library. Which source of compliance requirement is this?
options: A regulatory authority requirement
A statutory legal requirement
An industry-specific requirement
A company-wide standard
questions.explanation: Requirements that a company imposes on its own development tools, libraries, frameworks and protocols are company-wide standards. Regulatory, legal and industry-specific sources come from outside the company, from regulators, statutes and sector standards such as PCI.

questions.question: Which TWO items belong in the security requirements for an outsourced development vendor? (Choose two.)
options: Notification of vulnerabilities and incidents within an agreed time
A requirement to brand dashboards with the vendor logo
Unlimited subcontracting without notice to the customer
The vendor preferred code editor and window layout
A right to audit the vendor secure development practices
questions.explanation: Vendor requirements address how the supplier builds and handles security: timely notification and the ability to verify practices. Editor choice and logos are irrelevant, and unlimited unannounced subcontracting would remove control over who touches the code.

questions.question: A data custodian, such as a database administrator, decides the classification of the data it stores.
questions.explanation: The data owner decides classification, while the custodian operates and protects the data according to the owner rules. Letting custodians classify data leaves no accountable business decision.

questions.question: A hardening baseline for the deployed system is normally written as a non-functional requirement.
questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements cover security, operational, continuity and deployment qualities. A required hardening baseline, supported platforms and installation privileges are deployment requirements and are tested like other requirements.

questions.question: An enterprise architect wants a risk-driven framework that traces business requirements down to security services and controls, with views for the business, the architect, the designer and the builder. Which is the best fit?
options: The Open Web Application Security Project Top 10 list of web risks
The Common Criteria assurance levels for evaluated products
The Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture (SABSA)
The STRIDE method for categorizing threats on a data flow diagram
questions.explanation: SABSA is a layered, business-driven security architecture method that derives controls from business requirements. The Top 10 is an awareness list, Common Criteria evaluates products against a Security Target, and STRIDE classifies threats rather than building an architecture.

questions.question: A purchasing workflow passes a request through a web tier, an application service and a payment service. Each hop re-verifies the caller and propagates the original user identity, so the payment service can see who really initiated the request. Which pattern is this?
options: Security chain of responsibility, where each link verifies and passes along the trust information
Single sign-on, where one login replaces the checks that every later service would otherwise make
Defense in depth through geographic diversity of the three tiers
Least common mechanism, where the tiers share one authentication component
questions.explanation: In a chain of responsibility each component takes its turn deciding whether to accept or refuse, and passes trusted identity context on to the next. SSO is about reducing logins rather than skipping later checks, geographic diversity is about location, and sharing one component runs against least common mechanism.

questions.question: A design uses a queue so a front-end service can hand work to back-end workers asynchronously. Which security concern is specific to message queuing?
options: Messages may be read, forged or replayed unless the queue is secured
The queue guarantees ordering, which means producers no longer need to be authenticated
Asynchronous processing removes the need to validate the content of each message
A queue is internal infrastructure, so only the front-end service needs authorization
questions.explanation: A broker is another trust boundary: anything that can publish may inject work, and anything that can read may disclose it, so access control, integrity and confidentiality of messages must be designed in. Ordering does not authenticate, consumers still validate untrusted payloads, and the broker itself must be access controlled.

questions.question: An enterprise service bus connects dozens of legacy services through web services. A review recommends validating message schemas and signing messages at the bus. What is the main reason for centralizing this?
options: Policy is enforced consistently at one chokepoint, not re-implemented per service
The bus becomes a trusted component, so backend services can drop their own authorization
Signed messages remove the need for transport encryption between any two services
Schema validation at the bus makes each service safe from injection in its own code
questions.explanation: A central enforcement point gives consistent policy and a place to log, but it does not replace defense in depth: services still authorize and validate. Message signatures give integrity and origin, not confidentiality, and bus validation does not remove injection flaws inside a service.
